title: Canary signals, statistical tests, and rolling-window runbook for Optimize quality gates
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Problem: As Optimize rolls out model/quantization changes and promptset updates, we need a deterministic, actionable set of canary signals and a rolling-window runbook that prevents customer-impacting regressions while avoiding noisy false positives. This ticket defines the statistical tests, minimum effect sizes, sampling heuristics, and an operational playbook for automated and manual rollback decisions.
background: Current Optimize gating uses simple threshold checks (delta > X) on a handful of metrics. Engineering and SRE report too many spurious alerts during traffic spikes and A/B tests, and PMs are uncomfortable with manual interpretation. We need a repeatable, documented approach that: 1) reduces false positives via proper hypothesis testing and multiple-comparison correction; 2) accounts for non-stationary traffic via rolling windows; 3) ties alert severity to customer impact and runbook escalation steps.
scope: In-scope: define canary metric set (quality/cost/latency), statistical test defaults (e.g., test type, p-value, multiple correction), rolling-window size defaults, minimum detectable effect (MDE) guidelines, sampling rules for promptsets, automated signal scoring logic, and an operational runbook for actions. Out-of-scope: implementation of UI pages in Console (separate ticket), backend export endpoints for raw prompts (privacy review).
out_of_scope: UI authoring for custom gates, on-prem-only config differences (handled in Private backlog), experiment framework rewrites.
deliverables: Canonical list of canary metrics and metric-level SLOs
Statistical specification document (tests, corrections, MDE) with worked examples
Sampling matrix for promptsets (strata and min N per stratum)
Runbook with automation hooks and manual escalation playbook
Acceptance tests and example signal dashboard queries
canary_metrics: Quality: prompt-level ROC-AUC, top-k match rate, BLEU-like normalized overlap for deterministic outputs
Quality proxy: hallucination rate (manual labels + heuristics)
User-facing metric: percentage of sessions with >1 bad response (derived)
statistical_spec: Primary test: two-sided Mann-Whitney U for non-normal continuous quality proxies; t-test when normality verified
Significance default: alpha=0.01 for primary metric; 0.05 for secondary diagnostics
Multiple comparisons: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across prompt strata and metrics
Minimum detectable effect (MDE): express as relative change (e.g., 3% absolute drop in top-k match at 80% power, default sample N guidance included)
Confidence intervals: bootstrap CIs for non-parametric metrics with 10k resamples by default
sampling_heuristics: Stratify promptset by intent/category and length bucket (short/mid/long)
Minimum per-stratum N = max(50, MDE-guided N); otherwise suppress stratum-level alerts and surface global metric only
Prefer recent traffic: rolling window weighted average with half-life of 7 days (configurable)
Sample deterministically for reproducibility (seeded sampling key derived from prompt id + model version)
Customer-facing canaries: optionally run per-customer with higher MDE and reduced alpha to avoid overfitting
alert_scoring_and_actions: Signal score computed as signed z-score adjusted by stratum weight and corrected p-value
Severity tiers: P0 (automatic rollback eligible), P1 (paginated alert + on-call review), P2 (dashboard anomaly)
Automatic rollback trigger: primary metric passes P0 criteria AND effect size > configured MDE AND sustained across two sequential rolling windows
Soft-fail: degrade to cheaper model variant when latency or cost exceeds thresholds without quality loss
runbook_steps: Step 0: Automated pre-filter: ignore alerts originating from <N requests or a small customer cohort unless marked customer-impact high
Step 1: On-call runbook ingestion: link alert to dashboard, include sample prompts and decoded outputs
Step 2: Quick triage (15m): check for upstream infra incidents, data drift, or schema changes
Step 3: Validate signal with bootstrap CIs and per-stratum breakdowns
Step 4: If P0 auto-rollback criteria met, system triggers canary rollback and notifies stakeholders
Step 5: Post-rollback verification for 2 rolling windows; if stable, schedule RCA and release block
Escalation: include PM, SRE, and model owner; open incident if >5% user-facing error-rate increase
acceptance_criteria: Specification doc reviewed and approved by ML research, SRE, and Console PMs
A set of worked examples showing detection and non-detection for synthetic regressions (included in PR) must pass CI
Backend implementation exposes signal score and corrected p-value in API (contract documented)
Runbook automation successfully executes simulated auto-rollback in staging against synthetic regressions
Sampling matrix validated against three representative promptsets: assistant-chat, semantic-search, and code-completion
Performance: statistical computation completes within 30s for canary windows up to 100k samples
success_metrics: Reduction in false-positive alerts by >=40% (baseline monthly avg)
Time-to-detect true regressions <= 2 rolling windows (config default)
Percentage of rollbacks that are automated and revert within SLA >= 70%
Operator time spent per alert reduced by 50% after runbook adoption
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): implement tests, sampling pipeline, scoring; run on synthetic data (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 10% of Optimize traffic with P1 alerts only (3 weeks)
Phase 3 (broader): enable P0 auto-rollbacks and per-customer canaries where customers opt-in (4 weeks)
Phase 4: retrospective, update MDE defaults based on live signal; bake into Console UI in follow-up ticket
decision_log: 2025-02-18: Chose FDR over Bonferroni to reduce missed true positives (decision by ML Research)
2025-02-22: Default alpha set to 0.01 for primary metric after SRE risk review
2025-02-27: Adopted rolling-window half-life of 7 days to balance noise and responsiveness
open_questions: Should we enable automatic rollback for enterprise customers with dedicated models? (legal/contract considerations)
What default MDE is acceptable for hallucination proxy metrics where label noise is high?
Do we require per-customer opt-in for any data retention used for bootstrap sampling?

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overly aggressive auto-rollback could cause churn during transient infra events. Mitigation: require two consecutive windows + infra sanity checks before auto-rollback
Risk: Small prompt strata yield noisy p-values. Mitigation: suppress low-N strata and surface global signal; educate PMs on MDE limits
Risk: Compliance around storing sample prompts. Mitigation: redact PII and require Privacy sign-off for any raw prompt retention
